title: Batcher Pulse: continuous workload heartbeat profiler and safe parameterizer
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Build a continuous 'pulse' profiler that emits lightweight workload sketches (temporal histograms + token-length fingerprints) and a parameterizer that synthesizes conservative batching/caching recommendations which can be applied via staged canaries and automated rollback. Scope covers serving runtime sampling, heuristic ruleset, shadow-apply comparisons, rollout gates, and SLO/cost-based rollback triggers.

Background: Existing profiling is episodic and heavy-weight; teams lack continuous signals to react to workload drift. We need a low-overhead sampler that captures per-route heartbeat metrics (arrival distribution, prefix reuse ratio, KV-affinity score) and feeds a recommender which proposes safe batch_size, concurrency, and prefix-cache TTL adjustments.

Approach:
1) Runtime pulse collector (C++ agent in serving runtime) emits summarized sketches every minute: p50/p90/p99 inter-arrival, length distribution buckets, average KV reuse per request, and microburst counters. Payloads are tiny (<=1KB) and sent to the telemetry pipeline with route/model tags.
2) Temporal sketcher service (offline/nearline) aggregates windows (1m/5m/1h) and computes stability scores and trend deltas. Use EWMA smoothing and bloom-ish fingerprinting for prefix reuse to protect payload size.
3) Heuristic parameterizer: set of guarded rules that map stability + cost-savings estimate -> recommendation. Rules include KV-affinity aware batching (increase batch horizon only when KV reuse > 0.65), microburst dampening (limit batch growth when microburst_rate>threshold), and sequence-length aware concurrency caps.
4) Safety and rollout: every recommended config is first run in shadow mode for 24h (traffic mirrored) and evaluated by the regression checker. If shadow metrics satisfy cost delta and latency SLOs, the system creates a staged rollout plan (5% for 2h -> 25% for 3h -> 100% gradual), with automated rollback triggers.

Acceptance criteria:
- Pulse collector <1% CPU overhead on p99 path and <1KB/min per route network overhead.
- Recommender produces actionable suggestions for >=60% of high-volume routes in pilot.
- Shadow apply evaluation catches regressions and prevents unsafe applies in >= 95% of pilot recommendations.
- Rollback triggers correctly detect and revert when p99 latency increases >15%, error rate >0.2%, or cost-per-1k tokens increases >8%.

Telemetry & Alerts: New dashboards: 'Pulse Health' (ingest rate, sketch latency), 'Recommendation Outcomes' (accepted/rejected, shadow delta distributions), and 'Safe Apply Events' (applies, rollbacks). Alerting rules for missing pulses (>3 consecutive minutes) and failed shadow evaluation rate >10%.

Artifacts / Links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Batcher+Pulse+Design
- Prototype repo (GitHub): https://github.com/redwood-inference/batcher-pulse-proto/pulls/12
- Eval notebook (Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1BatchPulseEval

Open decisions:
- Exact thresholds for KV-affinity and microburst_rate need small-scale calibration (runbook to collect labeled routes).
- Whether to store sketches in long-term store for monthly cohort analysis vs. aggregate-only retention for privacy/cost.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Pulse agent adds overhead on tail path. Mitigation: sample only 1/10th of requests on p99 paths and fallback to aggregated-only reporting.
- Risk: Heuristics overfit to pilot tenant patterns. Mitigation: conservative defaults and a confidence multiplier that locks changes until repeated stability windows observed.

Next steps:
- Finish C++ collector instrumentation and no-op telemetry wire format (Ravi) — target 2026-03-05.
- Run 2-week pilot on internal 'sandbox' tenant and compare recommendations to manual config (Ava + SRE).
- Build shadow compare job and rollback automation (backend infra).
